title: Kestrel catalog search: products absent from locale-filtered results after a morning release window
domain: e-commerce catalog search indexing and change-data-capture pipeline
summary: Alderway Retail Group runs Kestrel, the catalog search platform behind six English storefronts. On Tuesday 9 September merchandisers reported that newly published products were absent from search and that some older products showed prior-week attributes. The record below is the incident file as it accumulated, divided into the four stages at which the responders actually held evidence.

entities.role: Retailer operating six English-language storefronts (en-GB, en-AU, en-IE, en-NZ, en-US, en-CA).

evidence.text: Pipeline reference, current at intake: the catalog database feeds change-data-capture into the Kafka topic catalog.changes on cluster msk-cat-a (12 partitions, keyed by SKU, ordering preserved per key; partition count may be increased but never reduced); the Kestrel-Indexer fleet of 24 pods consumes it and writes into the Quill index catalog_v7 (12 primary shards, one replica each, 9 data nodes, 1 s refresh interval); Kestrel-API queries catalog_v7; Bracken caches storefront responses; six English storefronts (en-GB, en-AU, en-IE, en-NZ, en-US, en-CA) are served from the same index with a locale filter. The runbook notes that an index alias swap discards the previous index, and that document _id values and _version history exist only in the live index.

09:12, Tuesday 9 September. Marissa Vogel opens INC-4417: products published on the UK storefront this morning do not appear in search, and several older products show last week's price and availability.

09:18. A direct request to Kestrel-API for SKU AW-90412 with the locale filter en-GB returns zero hits. The same SKU's product detail page, which reads from the catalog service rather than from Kestrel, renders current values.
09:24. The query is repeated with Bracken bypassed, sending Cache-Control: no-store to the origin host directly. Kestrel-API omits the SKU from its own response.
09:26. Every complaint so far has come from the UK desk. No reports have arrived from the AU, IE, NZ, US or CA desks.
09:30. Kestrel-API p99 query latency rose from a seven-day baseline of 180 ms to 640 ms between 09:05 and 09:35. p50 latency held at 22 ms throughout.
09:34. catalog_v7 reports green with no unassigned or relocating shards. The endpoint reports allocation state only; it reports neither segment age nor refresh progress.
10:02. Consumer-group kestrel-indexer lag on partitions 7 to 11 of catalog.changes rises from roughly 2,000 messages to 1,940,000 messages beginning at 08:44, and is still climbing.
10:05. The fleet was reduced from 24 pods to 18 pods at 08:30 after a thirty-minute window below the CPU target.

10:11. Changes for the morning: a rolling broker patch on msk-cat-a completed at 08:40; indexer release 4.21 was canaried to 3 of the 24 pods at 08:55 by Wen Li; the Bracken catalog response lifetime was raised from 30 s to 60 s the previous Friday.
10:14. Wen Li's notes for release 4.21 read: 'observability and log-format changes only; no change to indexing behaviour.'
10:26. Data node quill-d4 recorded an 11.3 s old-generation garbage-collection pause at 09:22.
10:51. A degraded point of presence is listed in eu-west-1 from 08:50 to 09:40.

evidence.source: Indexer service metrics and pod logs
evidence.text: 12:40. The processed-events counter reads 612,410 events for 08:00 to 11:00, against a seven-day median of 598,200 for the same window. The counter is a fleet-wide aggregate and is not broken out by partition. Pod logs for the window contain no bulk-rejection errors and no unhandled exceptions.

13:05. Median ingest-to-visible latency is 4.1 s and p95 is 9.8 s across 08:00 to 12:00, unchanged from the prior week. The probe's canary row is keyed to a fixed SKU that maps to partition 3, so the probe does not sample partitions 7 to 11.

13:30. A rejection spike runs from 09:05 to 09:40, with mapper_parsing_exception raised on the field fulfilment_class. The panel plots a sampled error rate; it carries neither absolute rejected-document counts nor document identifiers.

14:10. Locale breakdown of 1,204 sampled customer-visible misses: en-GB 38%, en-AU 21%, en-IE 14%, en-NZ 11%, en-US 9%, en-CA 7%. For each affected SKU exactly one locale still returns a hit, and which locale that is differs from SKU to SKU.

14:45. Affected SKUs are distributed evenly across all 12 primary shards; primary and replica document counts are identical for every shard; the refresh interval is the configured 1 s on all 9 data nodes.

16:20. catalog_v7 holds 2,973,640 documents against 3,014,880 active SKU-locale rows in the catalog database, a shortfall of 41,240. Catalog records show 8,248 SKUs published or re-published between 08:55 and 16:00.
17:02. Indexer 4.21 differs from 4.20 in exactly one production dependency: catalog-keys 2.5.3 to 2.6.0. The 2.6.0 changelog entry reads 'normalise locale tags before key derivation.'

Friday. Lattice resolves partition leadership from a topic-metadata cache that is refreshed only when the exporter starts. After the 08:40 broker patch the cache held pre-restart leader assignments, so lag for partitions 7 to 11 was computed against replica offsets. Observability formally withdraws the lag figures published for 08:40 to 18:00 on 9 September and reissues them: recomputed peak lag for the window is 1,912 messages, about 4 s of delay.

Friday. Replay of the Quill bulk-rejection log for 09:05 to 09:40 recovers 312 rejected documents, all from the seasonal-promo feed. None of the 8,248 SKUs published or re-published during the incident appears in the rejected set.

Saturday. 8,248 documents in catalog_v7 carry _id values of the form sha1(sku|'en'), an identity shape release 4.20 never produced. Each such document holds a single regional value in its locale field, and for those SKUs no documents exist for the other five English locales.

Saturday. In catalog-keys 2.6.0, documentId(sku, locale) derives its key from languageOf(locale); languageOf returns the primary language subtag, so en-GB, en-AU, en-IE, en-NZ, en-US and en-CA all reduce to 'en'. The three canary pods running release 4.21 were the only writers using 2.6.0.

Saturday. Replica apply-lag samples for catalog-db-ro-2, the read replica the indexer reads row bodies from, are unavailable: that metric is kept only in the 24-hour raw tier and the window is five days old. The indexer's source-row updated_at debug logging is disabled by default and was not enabled at any point during the incident. No other record of source-row freshness was retained.

Saturday. Access logs for the window do not record result-set truncation, and the shed-response counter was introduced in Kestrel-API 4.22, deployed on 18 September, after the window. No stored record distinguishes a truncated response from a complete one during the latency excursion.

Saturday. The 09:05 to 09:35 latency excursion remains unattributed. No Kestrel-API or Quill change is recorded in that interval beyond the items already listed, and no further data for the interval was retained.

hypotheses.text: Consumer lag on catalog.changes partitions delayed the indexer, so index contents trailed the catalog during the window.
Mapping validation rejected bulk index requests after a field change, so a share of catalog updates never reached the index.
Stale segments on Quill replica shards, following refresh stalls on data nodes, served older document versions to queries.
The indexer's source read replica served rows older than their change events, so indexed values trailed the catalog rows.
The storefront edge cache retained catalog search responses past their intended lifetime and served them to shoppers.
Document identity derivation in the indexer collapsed distinct SKU-locale records onto a single index document.
Query-path load shedding in Kestrel-API returned truncated result sets to storefront queries while latency was elevated.

edges.text: The release 4.21 canary contributes to distinct SKU-locale records resolving to a single document identity.
Single-identity resolution contributes to locale-filtered searches omitting affected SKUs.
The broker patch contributes to Lattice reporting lag against pre-restart partition leadership.
The reported lag figures contribute to triage treating consumer lag as the working explanation.
Consumer lag on partitions 7 to 11 contributes to search results trailing the catalog.
Bulk rejections on fulfilment_class contribute to locale-filtered searches omitting affected SKUs.
The fleet reduction at 08:30 contributes to consumer lag on partitions 7 to 11.
The raised edge-cache response lifetime contributes to search results trailing the catalog.
The p99 latency excursion contributes to truncated result sets reaching storefront queries.
Locale-tag reduction in catalog-keys 2.6.0 mediates the release's effect on document identity.

actions.text: Raise catalog.changes from 12 to 48 partitions and increase indexer consumer parallelism to clear the reported backlog.
Rebuild catalog_v7 from a full catalog scan on the current indexer build and swap the search alias to the new index.
Hold the release 4.21 canary, pin all indexer pods to release 4.20, and re-check the affected SKUs in each storefront locale.
Restore the offset exporter's topic-metadata refresh and re-baseline the consumer-lag dashboard from the reissued figures.
Lower the Bracken catalog response lifetime from 60 seconds to 5 seconds across the storefront edge cache fleet.
Add the fulfilment_class field to the catalog_v7 mapping and replay the seasonal-promo documents rejected in the window.
Enable the indexer's source-row timestamp logging and retain the output for the next fourteen days of catalog traffic.
Extend the storefront search fallback to return default-locale results whenever a locale-filtered query yields no rows.
